bullets: OpenAI closed a $122B round at an $852B valuation in March; Anthropic raised ~$65B at ~$965B in spring.
Both labs made early-June confidential IPO filings; no public sign of financial distress.
A July 30 third-party tracker put OpenAI annualized revenue near $43B.
Anthropic's last public run-rate was still ~$47B (May); no July funding or solvency stress.
Polymarket bankruptcy markets opened Sep 17, pricing each lab's bankruptcy odds in the mid-teens to ~17%.
Reports on heavy 2026–2028 compute burn sharpened scrutiny of both labs' cash needs.
Bloomberg: OpenAI in talks with UAE funds (incl. MGX) and BlackRock to anchor a $30B+ round at ~$1.4T pre-money; IPO pushed to 2027.
Anthropic reported to be preparing an IPO as soon as November.
OpenAI told investors 2026 revenue would be ~$50B, well below the ~$70B run-rate signaled weeks earlier (Guardian, Oct 9).
The $30B OpenAI raise and Anthropic's expected November IPO both remained on track.
Anthropic told investors Q3 revenue rose 45% to $16.8B and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis (Reuters, Oct 14); it plans to file publicly on Oct 26 for a mid-November IPO (IFR).
OpenAI's ~$30B raise at ~$1.4T was still in talks with no term sheet; PitchBook put fair value near $1T as losses keep growing.

Anthropic made its S-1 public on Oct 26 (Nasdaq: ANT): H1 2026 revenue of $16.3B, up ~14x, with an implied ~85% gross margin, ~900% net revenue retention and just $6.2B of debt; most of its $80.7B H1 net loss was a non-cash convertible-note revaluation (CNBC).

The filing also showed ~$266B of noncancelable compute purchase commitments plus ~$321B of lease obligations, and flagged possible material revenue losses from its Pentagon dispute; the IPO could top SpaceX's record $86B raise and would beat OpenAI to market (AP).
